questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code acquires the locks for a transfer between two accounts, in terms of whether concurrent transfers can get stuck? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A transfer is requested for more than the source account holds. What is the state of the two accounts and their monitors after the call?
choices: The destination is credited first and then the credit is reversed in a finally block.
The monitors stay held until the caller retries with a smaller amount.
The source is debited to zero and the remainder is rejected.
InsufficientFundsException propagates, neither balance has changed, and both monitors are released.

questions.prompt: transfer() appends to the audit trail after the account monitors have been released. What follows from that?
choices: The audit trail can list entries in a different order than the balance changes were applied, but no thread ever waits for the audit lock while holding an account monitor.
A transfer can succeed without an audit entry if the audit lock is contended.
The audit trail is guaranteed to be in exactly the order the balances were changed.
Readers of auditSnapshot() block every transfer for the duration of the copy.

questions.prompt: totalHeld() is called while transfers are running. Each balanceMinor() call is synchronized. What can the returned total look like?
choices: It is always exactly the sum of all balances at one instant, because each read is synchronized.
It can be wrong, for example missing or double counting an amount that moves between two accounts while the loop runs.
It always equals the sum at the start of the call, because the loop iterates a snapshot.
It throws ConcurrentModificationException if a transfer happens during the loop.
